task: #139 Phase 4 — truthful week-2 monitoring information semantics
frozen_semantic_rule: Monitoring capture history MUST NOT claim a historical first-release timestamp it does not know. The only event capture-time monitoring may assert is: A NEW OBSERVATION / VALUE BECAME VISIBLE TO THIS MONITORING DECISION SET.

reproduced_behavior_on_current_main: build_information_set_delta therefore classified every week NO_NEW_INFORMATION
a genuinely newer monthly observation moved cyclical factor scores
the real multi-week monitoring loop could never produce week 2 once data changed

semantic_options_considered.reason: invents a first-release timestamp the source never supplied; violates capture_time != first_release_time

semantic_options_considered.option: emit NEW_OBSERVATION events from capture-time data
semantic_options_considered.reason: NEW_OBSERVATION is read downstream as first-release evidence; capture-time monitoring cannot know it is the first release

semantic_options_considered.option: relax the synthetic-movement guard for the monitoring lane
semantic_options_considered.reason: destroys the accepted protection against fabricated movement; Missing/Unknown would become tunable

semantic_options_considered.option: no-op: keep week-2 blocked until a formal release-events authority exists
semantic_options_considered.reason: the monitoring product is dead in week 2 while its information truthfully changed; the ledger item explicitly asked for closure

semantic_options_considered.option: derive a monitoring-only OBSERVED_UPDATE event from canonical observation-identity differences between the current decision set and the causal prior snapshot
semantic_options_considered.reason: truthful (visibility, not release), derived from persisted canonical state, needs no invented timestamp, preserves the guard

implemented_contract.event_type: ReleaseEventType.OBSERVED_UPDATE (new enum member, MONITORING capture-time lane only)
implemented_contract.derivation: producer-side diff of per-series observation identities: current pack vs previous_snapshot.details['series_provenance'][series_id]['observations']
implemented_contract.information_key: (observation_date, value) — a re-capture of the same value with a later available_at is NOT a new information event; any newly visible value for a real observation_date is
implemented_contract.recorded_identity: {observation_date, available_at, value, source, source_series_id} for DB packs; {observation_date, available_at, value, source_ref} fallback for hand-built diagnostic packs
implemented_contract.note_format: monitoring_observed_update: a new observation/value became visible to this monitoring decision set at <available_at>; capture-time semantics, no publication timestamp asserted
implemented_contract.guard_interplay: observed-update factor ids join changed_by_release, so build_macro_state_delta keeps refusing any movement without an observed information event
implemented_contract.same_week_retry: unchanged: a retry copies the prior weekly deltas wholesale, so the same observation can never become a second information event
implemented_contract.fail_closed: if the causal prior snapshot does not record observation identities (pre-#139 snapshot), no update is claimed and genuine movement keeps raising SyntheticMovementError
implemented_contract.formal_lane: untouched: no formal ingestion, admission, or OOS surface reads or emits OBSERVED_UPDATE; MONITORING != FORMAL_OOS preserved

invariants_checked: observation_date is real (taken from the canonical row)
source/provider/source_series_id preserved (also re-validated for identity by the ported #138 fix)
no publication timestamp is invented (asserted by test b7_07)
same-week retry never becomes a second information event (b7_03, c2_14)
a newly visible observation in a later week supports a truthful information-set update (b7_02, b2_14, c2_06)
